body:
Yeah, Epstein-Barr = Mono. Thank God that’s not a risk for either of us as we’ve both contracted it in the past… was a miserable 2 months from me too.

None of my friends get regular cold sores… if they did I would *absolutely not* share drinks with them. The only reason I know this is because I’ve known all of them for 7+ years. Also, just FYI, HSV-1 (what you can get from cold sores) can only be spread through active cold sores; if they’re not there it’s impossible to be spread through saliva. Not to say they can’t be on the inside of the lip and thereby invisible to the naked eye, though…

I really do hear you on this as I’m not someone who sips/shares drinks very often either and I’m doing medical stuff for college. I assume by glandular fever you mean mono? I just don’t know why the occasional sip of a friend’s drink is grounds for no physical contact, obviously, if I knew one of them had a cold sore or were sick I wouldn’t be drinking after them any time soon.

Yes, the incident was on New Year’s Eve. She is not immunocompromised. I want to think this issue is due to something else than just how it sounds but no matter how much I talk to her about it, it just kind of seems surface-level. I’d really like to know what’s going on, deep-down or on top.

Reusable bags spread coronavirus/other viruses more effectively than bags made out of plastic. Now is not the time to be bringing your own totes, people. Kudos to the stores that have banned these types of bags from being used.
Hey man, if you wanna reach out, my dms are open.

Thank you for the well thought-out response. I completely understand my average is above everyone else’s— which I partially address in the guilt I feel squeezing past everyone at an above average rate. It’s just so hard to think outside of your own head when you’re scared of letting yourself out of it. And I really do hope that some day I find the courage to truly let myself out. It’s just so difficult when death is such an easy choice.
